[BAKCEND] Fix FP4 TMA descriptor selection for small block K (#11935)

Mixed FP8/FP4 matmuls with BLOCK_K=32 or 64 can propagate an MMA-only
padded shared-memory layout into a TMA descriptor. Reject unsupported
padded layouts during descriptor selection, including shared_linear
candidate matching, so these cases load packed bytes with a valid TMA
layout and convert to the existing MMA layout.

Add small-BLOCK_K coverage to the FP8/FP4 TMA matmul test and compiler
regressions for direct and shared_linear consumers. Validated on GB300:
all 36 TMA matmul cases pass, and the descriptor-encoding lit test
passes.

Related to #11930.

[triton_kernels] Fix gathered activation scale indexing (#11928)

When a ragged matmul gathers activation rows, the values can use a dense
TMA descriptor while their scales are stored in padded, per-slice
blocks.
Selecting scale offsets from the values' descriptor mode uses a dense
row
count that is undefined for ragged inputs, causing compilation to fail.

Select scale offsets using the matmul's ragged dimension. Require the
scale layout and matmul to share the same `RaggedTensorMetadata`
instance
so their row boundaries and padding agree, without synchronizing device
data on each call. Document this contract and the required scale row
order
for gathered inputs.

## Validation

- Added four cases to `test_gathered_ragged_act_scale_indexing` in
`python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py`: shared metadata, different
  block offsets, different row boundaries with identical block offsets,
  and separately created metadata with equal contents.
- Reproduced the original compilation failure and the missing metadata
  validation before the fixes. All four cases pass with the fixes on
  NVIDIA GB200.
- 56 additional GB200 checks passed, covering gathered inputs, uneven
and
  empty slices, strided scales, and dense, batched, and ragged layouts.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passed.

## New contributor declaration

- [x] I am not making a trivial change, such as fixing a typo in a
comment.
- [x] I have written a PR description following these
  [rules](https://cbea.ms/git-commit/#why-not-how).
- [x] I have run `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`.
- [x] I have added tests in
`python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py`.
- [x] I have not added any `lit` tests.

[GSan] Add write_once allocations (#11774)

This adds a special "write-once" gsan allocation. The rules here are
that they can be written exactly once, and read many times after being
written.

This means we only need to track for read-after-write violations, so we
can simplify the shadow cell to a single scalar write clock which is
1/6th of the size of a normal shadow cell. This allows us to track
byte-granularity while actually using less shadow memory than 4-byte
granularity normal allocations.

Also, this allows for a completely wait-free shadow memory access
pattern. This means we don't serialize accesses to those address.

I got codex to port the llvm back into inline asm which reverted some of
the slow down. It also found a more efficient mechanism for fp32 to fp8

Disable floating-point fusion by default (#11270)

Disable implicit floating-point fusion by default. Kernels can opt in
with
enable_fp_fusion=True, or applications can restore the previous default
with TRITON_DEFAULT_FP_FUSION=1.

Set TRITON_FORCE_DISABLE_FP_FUSION=1 before starting the process to
override both settings. Explicit tl.fma operations remain fused.

Preserve fusion-dependent arithmetic with explicit FMAs and targeted
kernel opt-ins. Enable fusion for the Hopper MXFP4 test because a ptxas
bug causes it to fail with fusion disabled.

[PIPELINE] Keep dependent loads after GDC waits (#11906)

The loop scheduler can place a load before an in-loop `gdc_wait()`,
allowing a PDL consumer to read data before its producer has finished
writing it.

Treat GDC waits like CTA barriers when deciding whether to pipeline a
loop. Loops containing a wait remain unpipelined; waiting before the
loop still allows pipelining.

Fixes #11905.

Implemented with Codex assistance.

[Frontend] Fix constexprs being prematurely to_tensor'd (#11913)

Our promotion rules state that a runtime value with an existing dtype
should take precedence over a constexpr value's inferred dtype. However,
by calling to_tensor before we pass the constexpr to semantic, this
context is lost and we may over-promote.
